page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, offering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at up to 4.2 GHz. Dedicated CPU allocation is paired with an extensive cache hierarchy, consisting of 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. The CPU features comprehensive instruction extensions, including AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), VAES, and SHA-NI for accelerated vector math and cryptography. Total system memory measures 768.0 GB, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage or discrete GPUs are bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight strong parallel throughput across multi-threaded and memory-intensive evaluations. The instance attained top-tier marks in PassMark CPU score (97,473.82) and Geekbench multi-core performance (21,854.0), alongside strong results in stress-ng multi-core testing. Uncached memory throughput demonstrates top-tier capability, reaching 509.22 GB/sec on large-block reads and 209.25 GB/sec on writes. Furthermore, the instance achieved 137.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 139.58 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng single-core (1,950.59) and gzip compression (31.22 GB/sec), sit in the mid-range category, reflecting a platform focused primarily on parallel scalability rather than raw single-core execution.

The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers a resource-dense configuration for large-scale operations without paying for specialized GPU hardware. Because local ephemeral disks are absent, persistent storage requires external remote Premium Storage volumes. This architecture is suited for enterprise relational database engines, large in-memory key-value databases like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference models that take advantage of integrated AMX and AVX-512 instructions.

There are no bundled GPUs or local disks, requiring network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier results in uncached memory bandwidth (509.22 GB/sec read, 209.25 GB/sec write), Geekbench multi-core, and Redis processing, reaching 137.56 million operations per second. The server fits high-capacity in-memory caches, enterprise relational databases, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, and vector-accelerated CPU inference tasks.
